Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:11:1.english: Shakhaht Beri - That is his name.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:12:1.hebrew: אשכחיה - רב פפא לרב הונא, דקא חפר וקייץ שרשין:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:12:1.english: He found him - Rav Papa found Rav Huna digging and cutting [the] roots.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:12:2.english: What is this? - Why [do] you cut [the trees down]?

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:13:1.hebrew: אמרי ליה כולהי - הבאתי לו ראיות הרבה שלא יקוץ:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:13:1.english: They all said to him - I brought him many proofs that he should not cut [the trees] down.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:1:1.hebrew: כדנייד נכתמא אפומא דחצבא - שאם יניחו כד על חומה, וכיסויה עליה, ינוע הכיסוי מחמת הרעדה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:1:1.english: Like the movement of the cover on the mouth of the jug - For if they place a jug on a wall with its cover on it, the cover will move because of the shaking.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:2:1.english: Raketa - That which is shaken out of the flax.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:3:1.hebrew: מאי שנא מזורה - בשבת, דחייב. ואע"פ שהרוח מסייעתו, חשיב ליה עושה מלאכה; אלמא גירי דיליה נינהו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:3:1.english: How is this different from winnowing - on Shabbat, where one is liable? Even though the wind assists him, [the Torah] considers him as having performed a prohibited labor; evidently, [the effects of the wind] are his own arrows.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:3:2.hebrew: היינו זורה ורוח מסייעתו - כי היכי דלענין שבת הוי כחו, לענין נזקין נמי כחו חשיב ליה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:3:2.english: This is the same as one who winnows and a wind assists him - Just as with regard to Shabbat it is considered his own force, so too with regard to damages he considers it his force.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:4:1.hebrew: ולרבינא מאי שנא כו' - בשלמא זורה ורוח מסייעתו, לא הויא ליה פירכא, דקסבר: ממונא מאיסור שבת לא ילפינן, דהתם מלאכת מחשבת אסרה תורה. וכה"ג מתרצינן ליה להא פירכא בב"ק, בהכונס צאן לדיר (ב"ק דף ס.):
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:4:1.english: And according to Ravina, what is different etc. - Granted, [in the case of] one who winnows and the wind assists him, [Ravina] has no refutation [of the comparison], for he holds that we do not derive monetary law from a Sabbath prohibition, since there the Torah forbade only "deliberate labor." And in a similar manner we answer this refutation in Bava Kamma, in the chapter "Hakones Tzon LaDir" (Bava Kamma 60a).

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:4:2.hebrew: גץ - אטנצייל"א היוצאת מן הברזל, כשהפטיש מכה עליו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:4:2.english: A spark - [In Old French:] *etincele*, which comes out of the iron when the hammer strikes it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:4:3.english: Liable - Even though the wind carried them.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:4:4.hebrew: ניחא ליה דליזיל - לחוץ, שלא ידליק את ביתו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:4:4.english: It is preferable to him that he go - outside, so that he will not set his house on fire.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:5:1.hebrew: סמוך לשדה חבירו - בין שדה הלבן בין שדה האילן. וטעמא — כדי עבודת הכרם, שכשיחרוש את אילנותיו לא יהא צריך להכניס מחרישתו לתוך שדה חבירו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:5:1.english: Near the field of his neighbor - Whether [the neighbor's] field is a grain field or a field of trees. And the reason is [that the distance must be] sufficient for the work of the vineyard: so that when he plows around his trees, he will not need to bring his plowing into his neighbor's field.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:6:1.hebrew: מעמיק - להן, בעל השדה, שיצאו לתוכו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:6:1.english: He must dig deeper - [below] them — the owner of the field into which [the roots] have extended.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:6:2.english: He cuts [them] - To a depth of three handbreadths.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:6:3.hebrew: והעצים שלו - בגמרא מפרש של מי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:6:3.english: And the wood is his - The Gemara explains whose [it is].

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:7:1.hebrew: אבל בבבל שתי אמות - שמחרישתן קצרה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:7:1.english: But in Babylonia, two cubits - For their plowing is short.

Rashi on Bava Batra 26a:9:2.english: But I have kept them distant - four cubits.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:11:1.english: I do not cut down, for Rav said, etc. - And if you ask: But we learned in our Mishnah that he cuts it down and gives [the neighbor] the money. And one can answer that it is possible to establish [that Mishnah] as referring to a non-fruit-bearing tree. But this is difficult, for we say in Bava Kamma, in the chapter "Hachovel" (92a), regarding those date palms that were weakening the vines: that he said, "Tomorrow bring me their roots." Evidently, because of damage to vines, one is permitted to cut down date palms. And one can explain that there it is different, for they weakened the vines excessively, until one tasted in them the taste of wine.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:1:1.hebrew: אפומא דחצבא - על פי' הקונט' קשיא לר"י: דאיך יהא האפדנא נייד כולי האי, עד שתתנדנד הנכתמא? דא"כ הבית קרוב ליפול! ולפי הענין משמע שהיה בנין חזק, שהרי מתוך העושר בנאה. ובמס' שבת (דף עז:) נמי אמר: מאי אפנדא? אפיתחא דין, שמאספין שם לדין; משמע דבירה גדולה היא. ונראה לר"י דכד ניידא נכתמא — כשאדם אוחז הכד בידו, שזהו דבר מועט הרבה — א"כ מתנדנד האפדנא, חייב להרחיק. ולריצב"א נראה שאין פ"ה דחוק, דבדבר מועט מתנדנד הנכתמא, שהוא דבר קל, אף על פי שהאפדנא אינו מתנדנד כל כך:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:1:1.english: "On the mouth of the jug" - Regarding the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], Rabbeinu Yitzchak found it difficult: How could the apadna shake so much that the nikhtema would be set swaying? For if so, the house is close to collapsing! And from the context it implies that it was a sturdy building, for he built it out of his wealth. And in tractate Shabbat (77b) it also says: What is an apadna? "At the entrance of the court," where people gather for judgment; this implies that it is a large palace. And it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that [the phrase] "when the nikhtema sways" [refers to the case] where a person holds the jug in his hand, which is a very slight thing; so if the apadna sways [to that degree], he must distance [the tree]. But to the Ritzba it appears that Rashi's explanation is not forced, for the nikhtema sways from a slight thing, since it is a light object, even though the apadna does not sway so much.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:2:1.hebrew: זיקא הוא דקא ממטי לה - קשיא לר"י: דליחייב משום אש, מידי דהוה אאבנו וסכינו ומשאו שהניחן בראש גגו ונפלו ברוח מצויה והזיקו, דחייב משום אש, כדאמר בפ"ק דב"ק (דף ו.). והכא דאמטי ליה ברוח מצויה איירי, מדפריך עלה מ"זורה ורוח מסייעו" — דאיירי ברוח מצויה, כדמשמע בהכונס (שם דף ס. ושם) גבי "ליבה וליבתו הרוח"; ומדפריך מגץ היוצא מתחת הפטיש, דהיינו ברוח מצויה דחייב משום אש, דגבי אש קתני לה בהכונס. ואומר ר"י דלא דמי לאש, דאין חייב משום אש אלא כשעשה האדם את האש לבדו, כדכתיב "המבעיר את הבערה", בלא סיוע הרוח, ואח"כ הולכת על ידי רוח מצויה. אבל הכא אין עושה לבדו כל עיקר, אלא ע"י הרוח, דאי לאו רוח לא הוה רקתא אזלא כל עיקר, ודמי ל"ליבה וליבתו הרוח" דפטור. והיינו דמשני כי פריך בסמוך "מ"ש מגץ" — דהוה סלקא דעתך דדמי ממש לגץ; ומשני: התם ניחא ליה דליזל, ומתכוין להכות בכח עד שיצא הגץ ומתרחק בלא שום זיקא, וחייב משום אש על מה שגומר והולך על ידי רוח מצויה. אבל הכא לא ניחא ליה דתיזל — כלומר, ואינו מכה בכח, ואי לאו רוח אין הרקתא הולכת כלל. וא"ת: מ"מ יהא חייב להרחיק, מידי דהוה אגורן דמתניתין דחייב להרחיק, אע"ג דזיקא ממטי ליה? וי"ל: דמתני' כרבנן, והכא איירי אליבא דר' יוסי דלא מחייב אלא בגירי דיליה. והא דפריך מגץ ולא מצי לאוקמי ההיא דגץ כרבנן — משום דלא פליגי רבי יוסי ורבנן לענין חיוב תשלומין, אלא לענין הרחקה. וא"ת: מאי שנא מנמייה, דאפילו לר' יוסי מרחיקין, אע"ג דהיא גופה ממטיא נפשה, כמר בר רב אשי? ומיהו התם משום דזימנין דבהדי דנח כו' כדקאמר לעיל. אבל קשה מעורבין לעיל (בבא בתרא דף כג.), דאמר רב יוסף "אפיקו לי קורקור מהכא". וי"ל דגמרא לא סבר לה כרבינא, דר"ת פוסק כמר בר רב אשי וכאמימר. ועוד אומר ר"י דבעלי חיים שאני, דחמירי טפי מרוח, דכח אחר מעורב בהן, כדאמרינן בבבא קמא (דף ו.):
Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:2:1.english: "It is the wind that carries it" - This is difficult for Rabbi Yitzchak (the Ri): Why should he not be liable on account of fire, just as in the case of one's stone, knife, or load that he placed on top of his roof, and they fell due to an ordinary wind and caused damage, where he is liable on account of fire, as stated in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (6a)? And here, [the Gemara] is speaking of [a chip] that the ordinary wind carried, since it challenges it from [the case of] "one who winnows and the wind assists him" — which is speaking of an ordinary wind, as is implied in [the chapter] Hakones (60a, there) regarding "he fanned it and the wind fanned it as well"; and since it challenges from a spark that emerges from beneath the hammer, which is [carried] by an ordinary wind, and he is liable on account of fire, since [the Mishnah] teaches that in Hakones in the context of fire. And the Ri says that this is not like fire, for one is liable on account of fire only when a person made the fire by himself, as it is written, "He who kindled the fire" (Exodus 22:5), without the assistance of the wind, and afterward it travels by means of an ordinary wind. But here, he does not act alone at all, but only by means of the wind, for were it not for the wind, the chip would not travel at all; and it is like "he fanned it and the wind fanned it as well," where he is exempt. And that is why [the Gemara] answers when it challenges shortly afterward, "How is this different from a spark?" — since it had entered one's mind that it is exactly like a spark; and [the Gemara] answers: There, he wants it to travel, and he intends to strike forcefully until the spark emerges and moves away without any wind, and he is liable on account of fire for what completes and travels by means of an ordinary wind. But here, he does not want it to travel — meaning, he does not strike forcefully, and were it not for the wind, the chip would not travel at all. And if you ask: Nevertheless, he should be obligated to distance [the tree], just as in the case of the threshing floor in our Mishnah, where he is obligated to distance [it], even though the wind carries it? And one can answer: The Mishnah follows the Rabbis, whereas here [the Gemara] is speaking according to Rabbi Yosei, who holds him liable only for his own arrows. And as for the fact that [the Gemara] challenges from a spark, and could not establish that case of the spark as following the Rabbis — [this is] because Rabbi Yosei and the Rabbis do not disagree regarding the liability for payment, but only regarding distancing. And if you ask: How is this different from a mongoose, where even according to Rabbi Yosei we require distancing, even though it carries itself, as Mar bar Rav Ashi [argued]? But there it is because sometimes, while it is [still] resting, etc., as [the Gemara] stated above. But there is a difficulty from [the case of] ravens above (Bava Batra 23a), where Rav Yosef said, "Remove the raven for me from here." And one can answer that the Gemara does not hold like Ravina, for Rabbeinu Tam rules like Mar bar Rav Ashi and like Amemar. Furthermore, the Ri says that living creatures are different, for they are more severe than wind, since another force is mixed into them, as we say in Bava Kamma (6a).

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:3:1.hebrew: מאי שנא מזורה ורוח מסייעתו - ורבינא לא חשיב לה פירכא, דסבר: כי היכי דלא גמרינן משבת לענין תשלומין, כדמפרש רב אשי בהכונס (ב"ק דף ס. ושם), דגבי שבת מלאכת מחשבת אסרה תורה, אבל הכא גרמא הוא, וגרמא בנזקין פטור — הכי נמי לא גמרינן מהתם שיהא חייב להרחיק. ומר בר רב אשי סבר: נהי דחיוב תשלומין לא גמרי' לענין הרחקה, דליחשב גירי דיליה — גמרינן שפיר, כיון דגרמא בנזקין אסור:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:3:1.english: How is this different from winnowing, where the wind assists him? - But Ravina does not consider this a refutation, for he holds: Just as we do not derive [the law] from Shabbat with regard to payment of damages — as Rav Ashi explains in [the chapter] "HaKones" (Bava Kamma 60a, there) that with regard to Shabbat, the Torah prohibited only a deliberate act of labor, but here it is an indirect cause (garma), and [for] an indirect cause in damages one is exempt — so too we do not derive from there that he must distance [the tree]. And Mar bar Rav Ashi holds: Granted, we do not derive the obligation of payment with regard to the requirement to distance [the tree], so that it be considered his own arrows — we do derive it properly, since [causing damage by] an indirect cause is forbidden in damages.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:4:1.hebrew: ורבינא מאי שנא מגץ - וא"ת: ואמאי קאמר ורבינא? לאמימר נמי תיקשי לענין חיוב תשלומין, מאי שנא מגץ? וי"ל: משום הכי נקט רבינא, דאמימר הוי מצי לדחויי דה"נ חייב לדידיה בתשלומין, דלגמרי מדמה לה לזורה, ורוח מסייעתו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:4:1.english: "And according to Ravina, how is it different from a spark?" - And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] say "and according to Ravina"? According to Amemar too, it should be difficult with regard to the liability for payment — how is it different from a spark? And one can answer: The reason [the Gemara] mentioned Ravina is that Amemar could have rejected [the comparison], [saying] that in this case too, according to him, [the person] is liable for payment, since he entirely likens it to one who winnows, and a wind assists him.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:5:1.hebrew: אחד גפנים ואחד כל אילן - מתוך פ"ה לעיל (בבא בתרא דף יח.) משמע דנקט "אחד גפנים" משום דשייך בהו כלאים, דהביא ראיה מכאן דכשיש גדר ליכא איסור כלאים, וזה סומך לגדר מכאן וזה מכאן. ואין נראה, דשדה חבירו דקתני הכא על כרחך לאו בשל זרעים איירי, דהא מוקמינן בגמרא דמתניתין אילנות לאילנות וגפנים לגפנים; אבל אילנות לגפנים בעי טפי משום ציפרי, ומהאי טעמא גפנים לזרעים בעי טפי. אלא דנראה דנקט "אחד גפנים ואחד כל אילן" דלא תיסוק אדעתיה למימר דשיעור ארבע אמות דמתניתין דוקא בגפנים, שמצינו בהם שיעור זה במקום אחר לענין כלאים:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:5:1.english: "Both vines and any [other] tree" - From the fifth chapter above (Bava Batra 18a) it seems that [the Mishnah] mentioned "both vines" because [the laws of] diverse kinds apply to them, for [the Gemara there] brought proof from here that when there is a fence, there is no prohibition of diverse kinds, [as in the case where] this one leans against the fence from this side and that one from that side. But this does not seem right, because "his neighbor's field" that [the Mishnah] teaches here is necessarily not speaking of [a field] of seeds, since in the Gemara we establish that the Mishnah [speaks of] trees next to trees and vines next to vines; but trees next to vines require more [distance] because of birds, and for this reason vines next to seeds require more. Rather, it appears that [the Mishnah] said "both vines and any [other] tree" so that it would not enter your mind to say that the measure of four cubits in the Mishnah applies only to vines, since we find this measure for them elsewhere with regard to diverse kinds.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:7:1.hebrew: אבל בבבל ב' אמות - תימה: דבפרק המוכר את הספינה (לקמן בבא בתרא דף פב: ושם דף פג.) גבי קנה ג', קנה קרקע, דאמר רב יוסף: עובדא הוה בדורא דרעותא כו'. משמע מהתם דבבבל נמי בעינן ד' אמות, דבבבל הוה מעשה! וצ"ל דבההיא דורא דרעותא היה להם מחרישה גדולה כמו בארץ ישראל:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:7:1.english: But in Babylonia, two amot - This is difficult: In the chapter "HaMokher et HaSefina" (below, Bava Batra 82b, and there on 83a), regarding one who purchased three [trees], that he has acquired the ground, as Rav Yosef said: There was an incident in Dura de-Re'uta, etc. It implies from there that in Babylonia too we require four amot, for the incident occurred in Babylonia! And we must say that in that Dura de-Re'uta they had a large plow, like in the Land of Israel.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:9:1.hebrew: אבל בגפנים בעי טפי - והוא כשנטע דקלים כשהם גבוהים. אבל אם נטע גרעין — לא, דממילא קא גדל, ולא גירי דיליה הוא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 26a:9:1.english: But with vines, he needs more [distance] - And this is when he planted palm trees when they were [already] tall. But if he planted a seed, [the same does] not [apply], since it grows on its own, and it is not his own direct action [lit. "his arrows"].
